newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan drops charges against ethnic activists.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan drops charges against ethnic activists.

text.p: Pakistani authorities said on Thursday they had withdrawn criminal charges against 75 members of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) in the southern province of Sindh.

Two members of the Senate (upper house), five former parliamentary deputies, and dozens of other workers of the MQM will benefit from the decision of Sindh's caretaker government, a government statement said.

The withdrawal of the charges relating to prolonged violence in the provincial capital Karachi was recommended by a committee set up by the caretaker government earlier this month, it said. But it did not say whether the charges were found to be false.

The cases against the MQM members were registered in the past three years by the ousted government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto in a crackdown on violence, in which more than 100 people were killed in 1996 and about 2,000 in 1995.
Bhutto's government, sacked by President Farooq Leghari last month on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, blamed most of the violence on the MQM.
But the MQM, which speaks for Urdu-speaking Mohajirs who migrated from India at the sub-continent's partitition in 1947, accuses security agencies for the blood-letting.
